stories.title: Salesforce Acquires Cresta for a Reported $2.7B, Adding Voice AI to Agentforce
stories.body: On November 2, 2026, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, the voice-first operating system for customer experience, with the deal expected to close in Q1 fiscal 2028. Cresta's platform runs voice agents end-to-end, guides human representatives in real time, and analyzes every interaction; customers include Marriott, Comcast, and Alaska Airlines. The acquisition follows Salesforce's June 2026 purchase of Fin (formerly Intercom) for approximately $3.6 billion, making Salesforce the dominant buyer in the enterprise AI customer-service agent category within a single year.
stories.why: Any enterprise retailer evaluating Cresta, Fin, or standalone voice agents is now evaluating a Salesforce bundle — which raises the switching cost conversation and shifts the competitive map for every agent vendor in the room. A Graas seller can use this to show that the consolidation wave validates the category and creates urgency to lock in architecture decisions before the market narrows further.

stories.title: Neo4j Launches Context Engine to Give Enterprise AI Agents a Shared Knowledge Layer
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced the Neo4j Context Engine, a reusable, shared substrate that lets AI agents consistently reason over enterprise knowledge, including a predefined six-layer Business Ontology that maps an organization's processes, data, and AI assets into a graph. The product includes a graph-native memory layer that gives agents memory and reinforced learning from past decisions, plus decision tracking that logs agent reasoning as a permanent record. Neo4j positions the Context Engine as the architecture enterprises must build before agents can be trusted to act reliably on business data.
stories.why: This is a named architecture commitment from a major infrastructure vendor, shipping now — exactly the kind of proof point a seller can cite when explaining why AI agents fail without a governed context layer. It directly validates the data-foundation argument: agents stall in pilots because they lack a shared, structured substrate, and Neo4j is making that layer a purchasable product.

stories.title: McKinsey: 53% of Consumers Now Use AI for Shopping, but Companies Are Not Ready — 'Who Wins When AI Does the Shopping?' (Oct 2026)
stories.body: McKinsey's October 28, 2026 report — based on a June 2026 survey of approximately 21,000 consumers across 11 markets — found that 53% of consumers used AI for shopping in the past three months, and that in the US the share of AI users who completed a purchase directly through AI rose 70% year-over-year (from 10% to 17%). The report's headline conclusion is that consumer demand for AI-assisted shopping is rising faster than companies' infrastructure can support it, with McKinsey explicitly flagging that most retailers are not yet equipped to meet that demand. McKinsey argues that winning the AI consideration set now requires AI-ready product information: structured, machine-readable attributes, real-time inventory feeds, and verified customer feedback that agents can parse directly.
stories.why: This is the most current named McKinsey report on retail AI adoption and it frames the gap as an infrastructure problem, not a consumer-readiness problem — making it a direct conversation opener for selling data and context-layer solutions. The 70% YoY jump in US AI-completed purchases gives a seller a concrete urgency number for any retail or CPG enterprise still in pilot mode.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Boosts In-Stocks by 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60% in CPG–Retail Collaboration
stories.body: BCG published research showing that agentic AI can boost in-stocks by 2–4% and planning productivity by over 60% for CPG companies and retailers by enabling synchronized, constraint-aware supply chain decision-making between trading partners. In the BCG model, an agent monitors store- and DC-level inventory signals against sell-through velocity and proactively generates replenishment recommendations before the retailer's own cycle would catch a looming stockout, while a separate constraint-escalation agent evaluates substitute materials and ranks options by cost, lead time, and service-level impact. BCG's May 2026 Executive Perspectives on supply chain further noted that AI-related incidents rose 21% from 2024 to 2025, and that 69% of executives say agentic AI requires new governance — underscoring that outcome gains depend on auditable, explainable agent decisions.
stories.why: BCG's named outcome numbers (2–4% in-stock improvement, 60%+ productivity) are the kind of proof points that move a CFO conversation from 'interesting' to 'budgeted' — and they are attached to the exact workflows (replenishment, constraint resolution) that retail and CPG enterprises are piloting right now. The governance caveat (69% say agents require new controls) is a direct opening to discuss why a governed context and data layer is a prerequisite, not an add-on.

stories.title: Sierra Passes $400M ARR and $15.8B Valuation; Decagon Reportedly Exploring a Sale at $100M ARR
stories.body: Sierra raised $950 million at a $15.8 billion valuation in May 2026, led by Tiger Global and GV, and by late October 2026 had surpassed $400 million in annual recurring revenue — up from $150 million in February — serving over 40% of the Fortune 50 on outcome-based pricing. Decagon, Sierra's closest pure-play rival, reached an estimated $100 million in annualized revenue by August 2026 and is reportedly exploring a sale, while its $4.5 billion valuation (set at its January 2026 Series D) now equates to 45x that revenue figure. Salesforce's acquisitions of Fin and Cresta within the same year mean independent enterprise agent vendors are narrowing to essentially Sierra and Decagon as standalone alternatives.
stories.why: Sierra's ARR trajectory ($150M to $400M in eight months) is the clearest market signal that outcome-based enterprise agent contracts are closing at scale — which both validates the category and raises the bar for what a buyer expects to see in a proof-of-value. Decagon's rumored sale process signals that even well-funded independents are feeling the gravity of Salesforce's bundling strategy, giving a Graas seller a clear frame for why architecture and vendor choices made today will be hard to unwind.
